must_show: A single youthful blue Guruvayurappan stands calmly at the center of a broad circular devotional composition. Around him arrange clearly separated symbolic emblems: an unlettered crown for Manu, a closed palm-leaf bundle for Bhrigu, a veena for Narada, a small praying boy silhouette for Prahlada, a graceful white celestial cow, a dignified eagle Garuda, a calm many-hooded serpent and a flowing river for Ganga. An abstract spiral of breath evokes sacred sound WITHOUT any written Om or letter. These are manifestations, not an assembly of duplicate gods. Keep animals anatomically coherent, do not hybridize them.

stanzas.alt: The Lord revealed through his manifestations

landscape.composition_override: Central standing Lord with a spacious crescent of emblems across the landscape.

must_show: One established youthful blue Lord sits at the center of an open temple courtyard. Three distinct small narrative groups illustrate generosity (a dignified royal donor offering a bowl to a sage), disciplined prayer (a seated practitioner counting a modest rosary), and devotion (a reverent listener near the Lord). A bow and quiver laid respectfully on a low plinth evoke Arjuna without a combat scene. These are symbolic allusions to Bali, japa, Arjuna and Uddhava, not literal simultaneous historical events. Radiant trees, river and life around the court express the Lord in all excellence.

stanzas.alt: Divine greatness in generosity, discipline and devotion

scene_brief.mode: three paths in one continuous devotional landscape
must_show: Left: an anonymous mature ascetic peacefully contemplating in a simple rock shelter, a closed unlettered palm-leaf bundle nearby
Middle: an anonymous householder mindfully offering food to another person as an act of duty, without money or market selling
Right: a small group of devotees singing and praying toward a modest shrine containing the established youthful Guruvayurappan form
Treat knowledge, action and devotion as coherent paths with different dispositions, not opposing sides

stanzas.alt: Knowledge, selfless action and devotion as three paths to the Lord

must_show: A modest wooden sailing boat crosses a symbolic dark-blue ocean. A dignified elderly anonymous guru in simple ochre clothing steers with a single rudder at the stern. One adult devotee in cream cloth sits peacefully in the boat with folded hands. A full cream sail catches a benevolent breeze shown as decorative flowing curves. One small blue Lord appears in a distant shoreline shrine as the destination and source of grace, not as a giant disembodied face. The boat has credible structure, occupants sit inside it, hands attach naturally. No danger or drowning.

stanzas.alt: The guru guides the boat across worldly existence

must_show: A dignified elderly renunciant in plain cream cloth sits peacefully beneath a tree after losing wealth. An empty open coin pouch and a broken storage pot rest far behind him. Two distant townspeople gesture impatiently, without physical violence or threatening weapons. The renunciant maintains compassion and balanced composure, hands resting naturally on knees. A small shrine of the blue Lord in the distance conveys surrender; no zodiac diagrams, planets with text, or claim that others caused his inner peace.

must_show: King Pururavas, a mature warm-brown man with dark wavy hair and a short beard, steps away from an ornate palace toward a modest shrine of the established blue Lord. His crown and rich cloak have been respectfully set on a stone seat behind him; he now wears a simple cream dhoti and muted maroon shoulder drape. Urvashi remains a small dignified adult woman in a fully clothed graceful muted rose sari on a distant palace balcony, a memory of attachment rather than a villain. No romantic embrace, misogynistic symbolism, sexualization, or humiliation. His gaze and folded hands turn toward devotion.

stanzas.alt: Pururavas turns from attachment toward devotion
